jin: Heads up — benchmark run this morning shows a new regression in the kernel selector during scale-up. When the load mixes short (8–16 tokens) and long (512+) requests we see an 18–25% latency tail increase at 95p during autoscale.

alex: Can you paste the harness command + which model/kernel variant you used?

jin: Ran against open-llm-7b, kernel_selector=v2.4. Command: `./scale-runner --mode=mix --short=0.6 --long=0.4 --qps=350 --duration=10m --warmup=60s --dest=dedicated-pool-us`

jin: Quick profile snippet (top functions):
```
20%  kernel_selector::choose_batch_shape
14%  kv_cache::lookup_miss_path
12%  runtime::copy_kv_to_device
9%   kernel_impl::fallback_dispatch
```

sam: Interesting that `kv_cache::lookup_miss_path` is 2nd — suggests cold cache behavior during the onramp. Did the run include explicit cache warmup?

jin: No explicit warmup this time — the idea was to test realistic production onramp. But the scale-up window seems to interleave short/long so kernel selector sometimes picks a latency-optimized kernel for the first slice then falls back for long seqs, causing extra synchronization.

maria: What's the failure mode? increased mutex contention? extra memcpy?

jin: From flame traces it's extra memcpy and gpu kernel fallback path (small->generic) triggers, causing serialized k-v uploads too. Also burst-credit consumption spiked higher than baseline.

alex: That matches a change in PR #3421 — we added a conservative batch-shape heuristic for v2.4 that prefers stable shapes over aggressive recompile. Could be misclassifying mixed-shape windows.

sam: Proposal: run an apples-to-apples comparing three setups: (A) synthetic steady short-only, (B) synthetic steady long-only, (C) mixed schedule with deterministic seed; each with explicit KV warmup run to reach >=90% cache hit before ramp. Measure 50/95/99 latencies, memcpy bandwidth, and kernel selection breakdown. Also run all three in a dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbors.

jin: Agreed. I'll create the test matrix. For KV warmup use `loadtool --kv-warm=1000 --seq=avg` then wait for metric `kv_cache.hit_rate >= 0.9`. Then start the scale-runner.

loadbot: Automated note: scheduled job `perf/mixed-kernel-check-200200` created, ETA ~30m.

maria: Add one more axis: kernel_selector=v2.3 (baseline) vs v2.4 (current) so we can attribute regression. Also capture GPU util and PCIe memcpy counters.

jin: Will do. If v2.3 doesn't regress then we should revert the heuristic or add a mixed-shape override.

alex: If revert, add a canary with traffic-split and short retention so we don't rollback blindly. Also consider a small change: prefer shape-hints from first N requests in an onramp to avoid oscillation.

am: btw @opsbot any chance we can provision a tiny dedicated pool for quick repro instead of waiting on capacity? :pray:

opsbot: Request accepted. Dedicated ephemeral pool `perf-ephemeral-3` created for 45 minutes.

jin: Thanks — I'll run the matrix and post a short triage thread with numbers + flame graphs.

alex: Thanks — if you find a small repro we can craft a unit test in the kernel selector. :thumbsup:
